summary: Ryuzan Nishimoto worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Enga Teramoto, Chishu Kitagawa (1916), and Chijo Kitagawa (1916).

Ryūshō Hikata specialized in Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Tokyo under Junjirō Takakusu (~1914–1917) and held posts at Kyushu University (~1925–1958) and Fukuoka Women's University (~1958–1963).
Ryūō Asahi worked in Buddhist studies. He held teaching posts at Toji and Koyasan University.

S. D. Laddu worked in Indology and linguistics. He held posts at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1960–1968) and the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute, where he served as Editor of Annals in 2002.

S. Krishnaswami Aiyangar was an Indologist and historian-archaeologist. After studying at the University of Madras (~1893–1899), he served there as Chair of Indian History and Archæology (~1914–1929).

S. Kuppuswami Sastri was a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He held posts at Presidency College, Chennai, the Government Oriental Manuscripts Library, Presidency University Kolkata, and Annamalai University, and was a member of the University of Madras.

S. N. Balagangadhara works in philosophy and religious studies. After studying at Ghent University (~1978–1989), he served there as Professor in Comparative Science of Cultures and Director of the Research Centre Vergelijkende Cultuurwetenschap (~1991–2017).
S. N. Savadi is an Indologist who studied under Parashuram Krishna Gode and held a post at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.
S. S. Janaki worked in Indology. She served as Lecturer-cum-Research Assistant at the University of Madras (1966–1968) and held a post at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute (~1971–1999).

S. Sankaranarayanan was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1986–1999) and the Chinmaya International Foundation (1999).

Sabine Löhr is an Indologist who studied at the University of Freiburg and the University of Hamburg, completing her doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen (~1996–2004). She served as a Wissenschaftliche Hilfskraft at the University of Hamburg.
Sadahiko Kariya is a Buddhist studies scholar who held posts as a professor of Buddhist studies at Chizan Senmon Gakko and as an assistant professor at Shuchiin University.

Sadajiro Sugiura specialized in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He studied at Rikkyo University (~1888–1893) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1895–1898), later holding a post at Rikkyo University (~1900–1942).
Saileswar Sen worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Calcutta (~1918–1920) and completed his doctoral studies under Barend Faddegon (~1922–1924).
Sakda Hemthep specializes in Buddhist and religious studies. He studied under Peter Harvey and completed an MPhil at Cardiff University under Max Deeg (~2010–2014).
Sakya Trizin works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Khenpo Appey (~1972), Tritsho Khenpo Rinchen, and Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama.
Sakyong Mipham is a Buddhist and religious studies figure. He studied under Chögyam Trungpa, Khenpo Namdrol, Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche, and Penor Rinpoche, eventually succeeding Trungpa.
Salila Kulshreshtha works in history, archaeology, and religious studies. She has held posts at Jawaharlal Nehru University and New York University Abu Dhabi.

Sallie B. King specializes in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies. She studied at the University of British Columbia under Leon Hurvitz until 1973 and became Professor Emerita of Philosophy and Religion at James Madison University (~1991).

Sally J. Sutherland Goldman is a scholar of Indology and linguistics. She studied at UC Berkeley (PhD 1979) and under T. Shrinivas Shastri and Shivaram Dattatray Joshi, holding a post at UC Berkeley from ~1981.
